messages.content: What is the change in entropy in Joules per Kelvin of a 1kg ice block at 0°C if it is heated to 100°C under 1 atmosphere of pressure?

function.name: entropy_change_calculate
function.description: Calculate the change in entropy for a mass of a specific substance under set initial and final conditions. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

substance.description: The substance for which the change in entropy is calculated.

mass.description: The mass of the substance in kg.

initial_temperature.description: The initial temperature of the substance in degree Celsius.

final_temperature.description: The final temperature of the substance in degree Celsius.

pressure.description: The pressure the substance is under in atmospheres.

message.content:
**Answer:**  
The total change in entropy for a 1 kg block of ice that starts at 0 °C and ends as saturated steam at 100 °C (1 atm) is **≈ 8.6 kJ K⁻¹**.

---

### How the number was obtained

| Step | Process | Heat transferred \(Q\) | Temperature \(T\) | Entropy change \(\Delta S = Q/T\) |
|------|---------|------------------------|-------------------|----------------------------------|
| 1 | Melting of ice at 0 °C | \(mL_{\text{fus}} = 1\,\text{kg}\times 334\,\text{kJ kg}^{-1}=334\,\text{kJ}\) | \(T_{\text{melt}} = 273.15\,\text{K}\) | \(\displaystyle \frac{334\,000}{273.15}=1.22\times10^{3}\,\text{J K}^{-1}\) |
| 2 | Heating liquid water from 0 °C to 100 °C | \(m c_{w}\Delta T = 1\,\text{kg}\times 4.18\,\text{kJ kg}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}\times100\,\text{K}=418\,\text{kJ}\) | Integral over \(T\): \(\displaystyle \int_{273.15}^{373.15}\frac{c_{w}\,dT}{T}\) | \(c_{w}\ln\!\left(\frac{373.15}{273.15}\right)=4.18\times10^{3}\times0.312=1.30\times10^{3}\,\text{J K}^{-1}\) |
| 3 | Vaporisation at 100 °C | \(mL_{\text{vap}} = 1\,\text{kg}\times 2260\,\text{kJ kg}^{-1}=2260\,\text{kJ}\) | \(T_{\text{boil}} = 373.15\,\text{K}\) | \(\displaystyle \frac{2.26\times10^{6}}{373.15}=6.06\times10^{3}\,\text{J K}^{-1}\) |

Adding the three contributions:

\[
\Delta S_{\text{total}}
= 1.22\times10^{3}
+ 1.30\times10^{3}
+ 6.06\times10^{3}
\approx 8.58\times10^{3}\,\text{J K}^{-1}
\]

Rounded to two significant figures, this is **8.6 kJ K⁻¹**.

---

### Quick reference values used

| Quantity | Value |
|----------|-------|
| Specific heat of ice \(c_{\text{ice}}\) | 2.09 kJ kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| Specific heat of water \(c_{w}\) | 4.18 kJ kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| Latent heat of fusion \(L_{\text{fus}}\) | 334 kJ kg⁻¹ |
| Latent heat of vaporisation \(L_{\text{vap}}\) | 2260 kJ kg⁻¹ |
| Boiling point of water | 100 °C = 373.15 K |
| Melting point of ice | 0 °C = 273.15 K |

Feel free to ask if you’d like the calculation performed via the provided `entropy_change_calculate` function instead!

Also specific heat capacities.

Given mass 1 kg. We need standard values: specific heat capacity of ice ~2.09 kJ/kg·K; water ~4.18 kJ/kg·K; steam (gaseous) ~2.01 kJ/kg·K? Actually specific heat of steam at constant pressure ~2.01 kJ/kg·K. Latent heat of fusion ~334 kJ/kg; latent heat of vaporization ~2260 kJ/kg. Pressure 1 atm.

1. Heating ice from 0°C to 0°C? Actually initial temperature 0°C. So no heating of ice before melting. But we might consider heating from 0°C to 0°C? No.

But we need to melt ice at 0°C: Q_fusion = m * L_f = 1 kg * 334 kJ = 334 kJ. Entropy change due to melting: ΔS_fusion = Q_fusion / T_melt. Temperature at melting is 273.15 K. So ΔS_fusion = 334000 J / 273.15 K ≈ 1222 J/K.

2. Heating liquid water from 0°C to 100°C: Q_water = m * c_water * ΔT = 1 kg * 4180 J/kg·K * 100 K = 418000 J. Entropy change: ΔS_water = ∫ c_water dT / T = c_water * ln(T_final/T_initial). T_initial=273.15 K, T_final=373.15 K. So ΔS_water = 4180 * ln(373.15/273.15) J/K. Compute ln ratio: 373.15/273.15 ≈ 1.366. ln(1.366)=0.312. Multiply: 4180*0.312 ≈ 1305 J/K.

Alternatively use Q/T average? But better use integral.

3. Vaporization at 100°C: Q_vaporization = m * L_vap = 1 kg * 2260 kJ = 2260000 J. Entropy change: ΔS_vap = Q_vap / T_boiling = 2260000 J / 373.15 K ≈ 6057 J/K.

Total ΔS = sum: 1222 + 1305 + 6057 ≈ 8584 J/K.
